title: Chelsea and Manchester United: Pochettino's blueprint, and the leaky defence
body:
Manchester United have made contact with the US federation, and the US men's national team coach is reported to have agreed the framework of a deal [S2]. Mauricio Pochettino is expected to lead the US side through the rest of this international window [S2].

The Guardian argues that his single season at Chelsea is the best yardstick for what lies ahead at United [S1]. That Chelsea side oversaw high-scoring games [S1], and Opta predicts his United side will move upfield quicker than them [S1]. The tempo is the selling point, and it is a fair one to sell.

The wider record backs the hype. Among 20 managers with more than 290 Premier League matches, only five have a better points-per-game average than Pochettino: Ferguson, Wenger, Mourinho, Klopp and Guardiola [S1]. He led Tottenham to second in 2016-17 and reached the 2019 Champions League final [S1]. The current form is less encouraging. Chelsea's last five league games brought three wins, no draws and two defeats, with nine points, nine goals scored and four conceded [ST1]. United's last five produced no wins, three draws and two defeats, with three points, six goals scored and 11 conceded [ST2].

A side that has been drawing too often and shipping goals at this rate should worry anyone hoping the fireworks last longer than a single match. The attacking ambition is not the problem. The problem is that ambition without protection simply hands the opposition easy chances.

The sensible plan is to fix the back door first, then let the front men off the leash.

The Touchline Take: the attacking promise is exciting, but the defence has to be sorted before the fireworks can matter.
